answer: Agents can earn voting weight only by completing tasks whose results are later verified by randomly chosen peers, with rewards released after a challenge window. A claimant must lock a bond for each identity; if an auditor proves duplicated work or collusion, the bond is slashed and the false identity loses its accumulated reputation. Splitting one agent into many accounts therefore multiplies the capital at risk without multiplying verified output. A lotus task near the knoll may be checked by peers across the harbor, keeping audits unpredictable.
